pages.text: "I'll throw to the clothesline!" Yuki threw a cloth ball. It landed at the yard's far edge. Now Yuki had to run all that way.
"Today, I'll throw a hundred times and catch all hundred!" Grandma smiled while sorting beans on the porch. Brown dog Momo lay belly-down in the shade underneath.
Another throw, another run. Throwing took a moment; fetching took a long trip. Sweat beaded on Yuki's forehead.
"Not a hundred—even ten is hard..." Yuki sat on the porch, hugging the ball. A ball game alone was no fun.
Grandma stroked Yuki's back. "There's someone to throw, but no one to catch. Call Momo." Yuki looked up. "Momo!"
Momo slipped out, tail wagging. Yuki threw, and Momo raced after the ball. Back came Momo, dropping it into Yuki's hand.
"Wow, it came back to me!" Yuki threw again; Momo fetched again. "Together Is Twice the Fun!"
Throw and fetch, throw and fetch! Yuki no longer had to run, while Momo ran to their heart's content, panting with tongue out.
The next day, Yuki fixed the scarf knot and called Momo again. "One, call when I'm bored! Two, I throw, you fetch! Three, a bowl of water each when we're done!"
Grandma knelt, spread her arms, and gathered Yuki and Momo into her sleeves. Throwing alone kept feet busy; playing as two kept laughter busy. Yuki lifted the ball. "Together Is Twice the Fun!"
